question: For a browser agent built on LangChain and wired to thinker the standard way (the one middleware line: proxy and hooks together), what does thinker cost or save against the same agent without it, and does the page rule add to the cut?
rule: All six tasks in bench/tasks/browser, written 2026-11-15 before any session ran, on a site generated from a fixed seed (bench/browser/site.mjs) that grades each task itself. Four act on the page in front of them, two (mixer-ratio, noisy-grinders) have to carry facts from one page to a later answer. Not chosen by any outcome. Every arm caches its prompt with LangChain's own middleware, so thinker is measured against an agent that already caches.
